ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADE$ are equilateral triangles. Connect $BE$, $BD$, $CD$, $EC$. As shown in Figure 1, if $\angle ADC=30^\circ$ and $AE=7$, $EC=9$, what is the length of $EB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that, $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADE$ are equilateral triangles,\\
$\therefore AC=AB, AE=AD$, and $\angle ADE=60^\circ$, $\angle EAD=\angle CAB=60^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle EDC=90^\circ$\\
Since $\angle ADC=30^\circ$, $AE=7$, and $EC=9$,\\
$\therefore ED=AE=7$\\
In $\triangle CDE$, $CD=\sqrt{EC^{2}-ED^{2}}=\sqrt{9^{2}-7^{2}}=4\sqrt{2}$,\\
Since $\angle EAD=\angle CAB=60^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle EAD+\angle DAB=\angle DAB+\angle AC$\\
Therefore, $\angle CAD=\angle BAE$\\
$\therefore \triangle EAB\cong \triangle DAC$\\
$\therefore EB=CD=4\sqrt{2}$, hence the length of $EB$ is $\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.
